slides.title: Health insurance until 26
slides.sub: You can usually stay on a parent's plan for years. Know the rules and the deadline.

slides.heading: The rule
body: You can usually stay on a parent's job-based plan until you turn 26.
That holds even if you marry, move out, leave school, have a child or aren't claimed as a tax dependent.

slides.heading: Why it matters
body: In 2025, 7.9% of people in the U.S. had no health insurance for the entire year.
Coverage through a job was the most common kind: 53.5% of people had it for some or all of the year.

slides.heading: When you turn 26
body: You get a Special Enrollment Period. It starts 60 days before you lose coverage and ends 60 days after.
Open Enrollment for 2027 HealthCare.gov plans runs Nov. 1, 2026 to Jan. 15, 2027.

slides.takeaway: Put your 26th birthday in your calendar now. You get 60 days on each side to find your own plan.

posts.caption:
You can usually stay on a parent's job-based health plan until you turn 26, even if you get married, move out, leave school, have a child or aren't claimed as a tax dependent. On a parent's Marketplace plan, coverage can last through Dec. 31 of the year you turn 26.

Why it matters: in 2025, 26.7 million people (7.9%) had no health insurance for the entire year.

When you lose that coverage, you get a Special Enrollment Period that starts 60 days before and ends 60 days after. Open Enrollment for 2027 HealthCare.gov plans runs Nov. 1, 2026 to Jan. 15, 2027.

Data: HealthCare.gov; U.S. Census Bureau (Sept. 15, 2026); CMS (Oct. 30, 2026).
